base_member_text: [L13,L16,L23] (MED/unchecked-command-failure) The script runs the executable and opens the report without checking directory-change or launch success, allowing a failed invocation to display an old report.

[L16,L20-L21] (MED/process-synchronization) Completion is inferred from all processes with the executable name rather than the launched process, so concurrent runs interfere and no test exit status is captured.
[L18-L21] (LOW/busy-wait) The tasklist polling loop has neither a delay nor a timeout and can spin indefinitely while a matching process remains.
[L13,L25] (LOW/working-directory) Both directory changes omit cd /d, so a SolutionDir on another Windows drive does not switch the active drive.
audit_member_text: [L13-L16,L25] (MED/working-directory) The script uses cd without /d and does not check whether it succeeded, so a solution on another drive or a missing directory leaves execution in the wrong working directory.

[L16-L23] (MED/failure-propagation) The asynchronous test launch never captures the test process exit status and opens ftnunit.html even after launch or execution failure, potentially presenting a stale report.

[L18-L21] (LOW/process-wait) The wait loop polls without a delay or timeout and matches every process with the executable name, so an unrelated or hung test process can keep the script spinning indefinitely.

adversarial.rationale: The entire batch file contains neither a drive switch nor a directory-change success check: lines 13 and 25 use plain cd, and line 16 launches from the resulting current directory. The ERRORLEVEL check at 20-21 concerns only tasklist/find after launch and cannot validate the earlier cd; repository-wide caller/build searches found no wrapper guaranteeing the correct active drive or an existing target directory.

base_member_text: [L13] (MED/build-path-mismatch) The script searches bin/ConfigurationName although the test project places executables under bin/win32/ConfigurationName or bin/x64/ConfigurationName.
audit_member_text: [L13] (MED/build-path) The executable directory omits the Win32 or x64 component used by xbeachlibrary_test.vfproj, so ordinary configuration names select the wrong build directory.
